verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating machines through its API and CLI, general programmatic resource management over HTTP and the pspace CLI, a stop state reached through auto-shutdown, and a selectable starting state at creation. A community user reports hourly VM billing. However, the evidence never explicitly documents start, stop, restart or terminate calls in the API/CLI, and never states that stopped machines stop incurring compute charges. missing for 10: explicit API/CLI start/stop/restart/terminate operations, documentation that billing stops for stopped/terminated machines, hands-on corroboration of programmatic lifecycle control.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Programmatically manage Paperspace resources using conventional HTTP requests.
Programmatically manage resources using the Paperspace Command Line Interface.
The auto-shutdown feature places your machine in a stop state after a predefined period of inactivity
When you create a new machine, you choose your machine type, operating system or custom template, disk size, region, authentication, starting state
